A failing rev-parse means\n    ``worktree_root`` is not a git worktree at all.\n    \"\"\"\n    toplevel = _run_git_text(worktree_root, [\"rev-parse\", \"--show-toplevel\"])\n    if toplevel is None:\n        return False\n    # If worktree_root and repo_root resolve to the same directory, they are\n    # trivially \"the same\" worktree.\n    if Path(toplevel).resolve() == repo_root.resolve() == worktree_root.resolve():\n        return True\n    # Otherwise, they must share the same common git dir.\n    wt_common = _run_git_text(worktree_root, [\"rev-parse\", \"--git-common-dir\"])\n    repo_common = _run_git_text(repo_root, [\"rev-parse\", \"--git-common-dir\"])\n    if wt_common is None or repo_common is None:\n        return False\n    # rev-parse --git-common-dir may return relative paths; resolve them\n    # against the respective working dirs.\n    wt_common_path = (worktree_root / wt_common).resolve()\n    repo_common_path = (repo_root / repo_common).resolve()\n    return wt_common_path == repo_common_path\n\n\ndef is_worktree_of(repo_root: Path, worktree_root: Path) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Return whether ``worktree_root`` belongs to ``repo_root``'s repository.\n\n    This public wrapper preserves the fail-closed comparator used internally by\n    :func:`safe_commit` while allowing preflight validation to reuse the same\n    git-topology authority.\n    \"\"\"\n    return _is_worktree_of(repo_root, worktree_root)\n\n\ndef _destination_ref_exists(worktree_root: Path, destination_ref: str) -> bool:\n    result = subprocess.run(\n        [\"git\", \"rev-parse\", \"--verify\", \"--quiet\", f\"refs/heads/{destination_ref}\"],\n        cwd=worktree_root,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        encoding=\"utf-8\",\n        errors=\"replace\",\n        check=False,\n    )\n    return result.returncode == 0\n\n\ndef _find_s\n"}],"details":{"status":"ok"}}}

resolve them\n    # against the respective working dirs.\n    wt_common_path = (worktree_root / wt_common).resolve()\n    repo_common_path = (repo_root / repo_common).resolve()\n    return wt_common_path == repo_common_path\n\n\ndef is_worktree_of(repo_root: Path, worktree_root: Path) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Return whether ``worktree_root`` belongs to ``repo_root``'s repository.\n\n    This public wrapper preserves the fail-closed comparator used internally by\n    :func:`safe_commit` while allowing preflight validation to reuse the same\n    git-topology authority.\n    \"\"\"\n    return _is_worktree_of(repo_root, worktree_root)\n\n\ndef _destination_ref_exists(worktree_root: Path, destination_ref: str) -> bool:\n    result = subprocess.run(\n        [\"git\", \"rev-parse\", \"--verify\", \"--quiet\", f\"refs/heads/{destination_ref}\"],\n        cwd=worktree_root,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        encoding=\"utf-8\",\n        errors=\"replace\",\n        check=False,\n    )\n    return result.returncode == 0\n\n\ndef _find_s\n"}],"details":{"durationMs":4,"status":"ok","stdout":"def _is_worktree_of(repo_root: Path, worktree_root: Path) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Return ``True`` iff ``worktree_root`` is a worktree of ``repo_root``.\n\n    Uses ``git -C <worktree_root> rev-parse --show-toplevel`` to confirm\n    ``worktree_root`` is inside *some* git working tree, then compares the\n    common dir of ``worktree_root`` and ``repo_root`` — if they share a common\n    ``.git`` repository, they are linked. {"type":"tool_execution_start","toolCallId":"ipython_9","toolName":"ipython","args":{"code":"# Look for the \"checkout ROOT\" / subdirectory contract language in spec + contract doc\ncontract = open(spec_dir+\"/contracts/checkout-ownership-cli-contract.md\").read()\nprint(contract[:6000])"}}
{"type":"tool_execution_update","toolCallId":"ipython_9","toolName":"ipython","args":{"code":"# Look for the \"checkout ROOT\" / subdirectory contract language in spec + contract doc\ncontract = open(spec_dir+\"/contracts/checkout-ownership-cli-contract.md\").read()\nprint(contract[:6000])"},"partialResult":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Contract: Explicit Checkout-Ownership Affordance\n\n**Mission**: `worktree-owned-root-3328-01KZRG01` | **Issue**: [#3328](https://github.com/Priivacy-ai/spec-kitty/issues/3328)\n\nThis contract defines the CLI/API surface the implementation phase (WPs) must deliver. It is a specification of observable behavior — exact flag names/wording are implementation-phase decisions the tasks phase may refine, but the request/response shape and refusal taxonomy below are binding.\n\n## CLI Surface: `spec-kitty agent mission create`\n\n### New option\n\n```\n--owned-checkout PATH   Explicitly declare PATH as a linked worktree this invocation\n                         owns. Validated via git topology (common-dir + worktree\n                         registry) before acceptance. Mutually exclusive with running\n                         from an unowned worktree without this flag (existing refusal\n                         is unchanged when this flag is absent).\n```\n\n### Behavior contract\n\n| Precondition | `--owned-checkout` supplied? | Outcome |\n|---|---|---|\n| CWD is the primary checkout | No | Unchanged — succeeds as today. |\n| CWD is the primary checkout | Yes, path == CWD | Succeeds (trivial self-ownership case, mirrors `safe_commit`'s `repo_root == worktree_root` contract). |\n| CWD is a linked worktree (any path) | No | Unchanged — refuses with today's `MissionCreationError` (\"Cannot create missions from inside a worktree…\"). |\n| CWD is a linked worktree, path is a validly-linked, non-nested worktree of the resolved primary | Yes, path == CWD | Succeeds. Mission files, coordination/lane refs land under `path`. Primary checkout and every other worktree remain untouched. |\n| Path is nested inside another worktree's checkout | Yes | Refuses. Error is structurally distinguishable as `NESTED` (see Error Taxonomy). |\n| Path's git common-dir does not match the resolved primary's | Yes | Refuses. Error is structurally distinguishable as `FOREIGN_OR_MISMATCHED`, naming both common-dirs. |\n| Path's `.git` file exists but its `gitdir:` target is unreadable/missing | Yes | Refuses. Error is structurally distinguishable as `BROKEN_POINTER`. |\n| Any underlying `git rev-parse`/`git worktree list` subprocess fails | Yes | Refuses (fail-closed, NFR-004) — never falls back to unvalidated acceptance. |\n\n### `--json` payload shape (success)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"success\": true,\n  \"mission_slug\": \"...\",\n  \"owned_checkout\": \"/abs/path/to/worktree\",\n  \"canonical_repo_root\": \"/abs/path/to/primary\",\n  ...\n}\n```\n\n### `--json` payload shape (refusal)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"success\": false,\n  \"error_code\": \"OWNERSHIP_NESTED\" | \"OWNERSHIP_FOREIGN\" | \"OWNERSHIP_BROKEN_POINTER\" | \"WORKTREE_INVOCATION_REFUSED\",\n  \"error\": \"<human-readable message naming the specific checkouts/paths involved>\"\n}\n```\n\n`WORKTREE_INVOCATION_REFUSED` is the existing (unchanged) refusal code for the no-opt-in case — this contract does not rename or restructure it (regression risk called out in plan.md IC-04).\n\n## CLI Surface: `spec-kitty next`\n\n### New option\n\n```\n--owned-checkout PATH   Same semantics as `mission create`'s flag. When supplied and\n                         validated OWNED, `next` roots per-checkout runtime state\n                         (feature-runs.json, merge-lock directory) at PATH instead of\n                         the ambiently-resolved primary checkout.\n```\n\n### Behavior contract\n\n| Precondition | `--owned-checkout` supplied? | Outcome |\n|---|---|---|\n| CWD is a `.worktrees/<name>` path (today's `require_main_repo` detects this) | No | Unchanged — refuses exactly as today. |\n| CWD is a generic linked worktree (today's `require_main_repo` does NOT detect this) | No | Unchanged — behaves exactly as today (ambient resolution to primary; NOT retrofitted into a new refusal — spec.md Acceptance Scenario, User Story 2 #4). |\n| CWD is a validly-linked, non-nested worktree | Yes, path == CWD | Succeeds. Mission decision resolves against the mission stored at the owned checkout; runtime-state files (`feature-runs.json` equivalent) are read/written under the owned checkout's own `.kittify/runtime/`. |\n| Nested / foreign / broken-pointer (same taxonomy as `mission create`) | Yes | Refuses with the same structured error codes. |\n\n## Error Taxonomy (shared by both surfaces)\n\n| `error_code` | `OwnershipValidationResult` (data-model.md) | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| `WORKTREE_INVOCATION_REFUSED` | `UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN` | Existing, unchanged refusal — caller did not opt in. |\n| `OWNERSHIP_NESTED` | `NESTED` | The claimed checkout is nested inside another worktree's own directory tree. |\n| `OWNERSHIP_FOREIGN` | `FOREIGN_OR_MISMATCHED` | The claimed checkout's git common-dir does not match the resolved primary's. |\n| `OWNERSHIP_BROKEN_POINTER` | `BROKEN_POINTER` | The claimed checkout's `.git` gitdir pointer is unreadable, missing its target, or a git subprocess failed while validating it. |\n\n## Non-Goals of This Contract\n\n- Does not define `#3128`'s post-ownership caller-vs-declared-workspace comparison (that guard consumes this contract's validated `OwnershipClaim` as an input, in a separate mission).\n- Does not add any new production `allow_worktree_context=True` call site (NFR-003) — `--owned-checkout` is a wholly independent, validated parameter.\n- Does not change behavior for any caller that omits `--owned-checkout` (C-001/C-002).\n\n"}],"details":{"status":"ok"}}}

When supplied and\n                         validated OWNED, `next` roots per-checkout runtime state\n                         (feature-runs.json, merge-lock directory) at PATH instead of\n                         the ambiently-resolved primary checkout.\n```\n\n### Behavior contract\n\n| Precondition | `--owned-checkout` supplied? | Outcome |\n|---|---|---|\n| CWD is a `.worktrees/<name>` path (today's `require_main_repo` detects this) | No | Unchanged — refuses exactly as today. |\n| CWD is a generic linked worktree (today's `require_main_repo` does NOT detect this) | No | Unchanged — behaves exactly as today (ambient resolution to primary; NOT retrofitted into a new refusal — spec.md Acceptance Scenario, User Story 2 #4). |\n| CWD is a validly-linked, non-nested worktree | Yes, path == CWD | Succeeds. Mission decision resolves against the mission stored at the owned checkout; runtime-state files (`feature-runs.json` equivalent) are read/written under the owned checkout's own `.kittify/runtime/`. |\n| Nested / foreign / broken-pointer (same taxonomy as `mission create`) | Yes | Refuses with the same structured error codes. |\n\n## Error Taxonomy (shared by both surfaces)\n\n| `error_code` | `OwnershipValidationResult` (data-model.md) | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| `WORKTREE_INVOCATION_REFUSED` | `UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN` | Existing, unchanged refusal — caller did not opt in. |\n| `OWNERSHIP_NESTED` | `NESTED` | The claimed checkout is nested inside another worktree's own directory tree. |\n| `OWNERSHIP_FOREIGN` | `FOREIGN_OR_MISMATCHED` | The claimed checkout's git common-dir does not match the resolved primary's. |\n| `OWNERSHIP_BROKEN_POINTER` | `BROKEN_POINTER` | The claimed checkout's `.git` gitdir pointer is unreadable, missing its target, or a git subprocess failed while validating it. |\n\n## Non-Goals of This Contract\n\n- Does not define `#3128`'s post-ownership caller-vs-declared-workspace comparison (that guard consumes this contract's validated `OwnershipClaim` as an input, in a separate mission).\n- Does not add any new production `allow_worktree_context=True` call site (NFR-003) — `--owned-checkout` is a wholly independent, validated parameter.\n- Does not change behavior for any caller that omits `--owned-checkout` (C-001/C-002).\n\n","stderr":"","kernelRestarted":false},"isError":false,"timestamp":1786462178981}}

Mutually exclusive with running\n                         from an unowned worktree without this flag (existing refusal\n                         is unchanged when this flag is absent).\n```\n\n### Behavior contract\n\n| Precondition | `--owned-checkout` supplied? | Outcome |\n|---|---|---|\n| CWD is the primary checkout | No | Unchanged — succeeds as today. |\n| CWD is the primary checkout | Yes, path == CWD | Succeeds (trivial self-ownership case, mirrors `safe_commit`'s `repo_root == worktree_root` contract). |\n| CWD is a linked worktree (any path) | No | Unchanged — refuses with today's `MissionCreationError` (\"Cannot create missions from inside a worktree…\"). |\n| CWD is a linked worktree, path is a validly-linked, non-nested worktree of the resolved primary | Yes, path == CWD | Succeeds. Mission files, coordination/lane refs land under `path`. Primary checkout and every other worktree remain untouched. |\n| Path is nested inside another worktree's checkout | Yes | Refuses. Error is structurally distinguishable as `NESTED` (see Error Taxonomy). |\n| Path's git common-dir does not match the resolved primary's | Yes | Refuses. Error is structurally distinguishable as `FOREIGN_OR_MISMATCHED`, naming both common-dirs. |\n| Path's `.git` file exists but its `gitdir:` target is unreadable/missing | Yes | Refuses. Error is structurally distinguishable as `BROKEN_POINTER`. |\n| Any underlying `git rev-parse`/`git worktree list` subprocess fails | Yes | Refuses (fail-closed, NFR-004) — never falls back to unvalidated acceptance. |\n\n### `--json` payload shape (success)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"success\": true,\n  \"mission_slug\": \"...\",\n  \"owned_checkout\": \"/abs/path/to/worktree\",\n  \"canonical_repo_root\": \"/abs/path/to/primary\",\n  ...\n}\n```\n\n### `--json` payload shape (refusal)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"success\": false,\n  \"error_code\": \"OWNERSHIP_NESTED\" | \"OWNERSHIP_FOREIGN\" | \"OWNERSHIP_BROKEN_POINTER\" | \"WORKTREE_INVOCATION_REFUSED\",\n  \"error\": \"<human-readable message naming the specific checkouts/paths involved>\"\n}\n```\n\n`WORKTREE_INVOCATION_REFUSED` is the existing (unchanged) refusal code for the no-opt-in case — this contract does not rename or restructure it (regression risk called out in plan.md IC-04).\n\n## CLI Surface: `spec-kitty next`\n\n### New option\n\n```\n--owned-checkout PATH   Same semantics as `mission create`'s flag. When supplied and\n                         validated OWNED, `next` roots per-checkout runtime state\n                         (feature-runs.json, merge-lock directory) at PATH instead of\n                         the ambiently-resolved primary checkout.\n```\n\n### Behavior contract\n\n| Precondition | `--owned-checkout` supplied? | Outcome |\n|---|---|---|\n| CWD is a `.worktrees/<name>` path (today's `require_main_repo` detects this) | No | Unchanged — refuses exactly as today. |\n| CWD is a generic linked worktree (today's `require_main_repo` does NOT detect this) | No | Unchanged — behaves exactly as today (ambient resolution to primary; NOT retrofitted into a new refusal — spec.md Acceptance Scenario, User Story 2 #4). |\n| CWD is a validly-linked, non-nested worktree | Yes, path == CWD | Succeeds. Mission decision resolves against the mission stored at the owned checkout; runtime-state files (`feature-runs.json` equivalent) are read/written under the owned checkout's own `.kittify/runtime/`. |\n| Nested / foreign / broken-pointer (same taxonomy as `mission create`) | Yes | Refuses with the same structured error codes. |\n\n## Error Taxonomy (shared by both surfaces)\n\n| `error_code` | `OwnershipValidationResult` (data-model.md) | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| `WORKTREE_INVOCATION_REFUSED` | `UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN` | Existing, unchanged refusal — caller did not opt in. |\n| `OWNERSHIP_NESTED` | `NESTED` | The claimed checkout is nested inside another worktree's own directory tree. |\n| `OWNERSHIP_FOREIGN` | `FOREIGN_OR_MISMATCHED` | The claimed checkout's git common-dir does not match the resolved primary's. |\n| `OWNERSHIP_BROKEN_POINTER` | `BROKEN_POINTER` | The claimed checkout's `.git` gitdir pointer is unreadable, missing its target, or a git subprocess failed while validating it. |\n\n## Non-Goals of This Contract\n\n- Does not define `#3128`'s post-ownership caller-vs-declared-workspace comparison (that guard consumes this contract's validated `OwnershipClaim` as an input, in a separate mission).\n- Does not add any new production `allow_worktree_context=True` call site (NFR-003) — `--owned-checkout` is a wholly independent, validated parameter.\n- Does not change behavior for any caller that omits `--owned-checkout` (C-001/C-002).\n\n","stderr":"","kernelRestarted":false},"isError":false,"timestamp":1786462178981}]}

These tests\nexercise :func:`resolve_ownership_claim` against REAL temporary git\nrepositories/worktrees (``tmp_path`` + real ``git init`` / ``git worktree\nadd`` subprocess calls) mirroring the house pattern in\n``tests/runtime/test_paths_unit.py`` and\n``tests/git_ops/test_safe_commit_helper_integration.py`` — no mocked git\noutput. See ``kitty-specs/worktree-owned-root-3328-01KZRG01/data-model.md``\nfor the entity/validation-rule model under test.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom dataclasses import FrozenInstanceError\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom unittest.mock import patch\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom specify_cli.core import checkout_ownership\nfrom specify_cli.core.checkout_ownership import (\n    BrokenPointerCheckoutError,\n    CheckoutOwnershipError,\n    ForeignOrMismatchedCheckoutError,\n    NestedCheckoutError,\n    OwnershipClaim,\n    OwnershipValidationResult,\n    UnownedNoOptInError,\n    error_for_claim,\n    resolve_ownership_claim,\n)\nfrom specify_cli.coordination.surface_resolver import WorktreeRegistryUnavailable\nfrom specify_cli.git.commit_helpers import is_worktree_of\n\npytestmark = [pytest.mark.git_repo]\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Fixtures — real git repositories, mirroring\n# tests/git_ops/test_safe_commit_helper_integration.py's `git_repo` fixture.\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _run_git(args: list[str], cwd: Path) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [\"git\", *args],\n        cwd=cwd,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        encoding=\"utf-8\",\n        errors=\"replace\",\n        check=True,\n    )\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef git_repo(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Create a real, initialized git repository with one commit.\"\"\"\n    repo = tmp_path / \"primary\"\n    repo.mkdir()\n    _run_git([\"init\"], cwd=repo)\n    _run_git([\"config\", \"user.email\", \"test@example.com\"], cwd=repo)\n    _run_git([\"config\", \"user.name\", \"Test User\"], cwd=repo)\n    (repo / \"README.md\").write_text(\"# Test Repo\\n\")\n    _run_git([\"add\", \"README.md\"], cwd=repo)\n    _run_git([\"commit\", \"-m\", \"Initial commit\"], cwd=repo)\n    _run_git([\"branch\", \"-M\", \"main\"], cwd=repo)\n    return repo\n\n\ndef _add_worktree(repo: Path, path: Path, branch: str) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Create a real linked worktree of ``repo`` at ``path`` on a new branch.\"\"\"\n    _run_git([\"worktree\", \"add\", \"-b\", branch, str(path)], cwd=repo)\n    return path\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# T002 — UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN (no claim, zero subprocess calls, NFR-001)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_no_claim_returns_unowned_no_opt_in(\n    git_repo: Path,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"``claimed_checkout=None`` returns UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN with no git calls.\"\"\"\n    with patch(\"subprocess.run\") as run:\n        claim = resolve_ownership_claim(None, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN\n    assert claim.opted_in is False\n    assert claim.detail\n    assert str(git_repo.resolve()) in claim.detail\n    run.assert_not_called()\n\n\ndef test_no_claim_error_for_claim_maps_to_unowned_error(git_repo: Path) -> None:\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(None, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n    err = error_for_claim(claim)\n    assert isinstance(err, UnownedNoOptInError)\n    assert isinstance(err, CheckoutOwnershipError)\n    assert err.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# T002 — trivial self-ownership (primary claiming itself) is OWNED\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_primary_self_ownership_is_owned(git_repo: Path) -> None:\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(git_repo, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.OWNED\n    assert claim.opted_in is True\n    assert claim.claimed_checkout == git_repo.resolve()\n    assert claim.resolved_primary == git_repo.resolve()\n    assert error_for_claim(claim) is None\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# T002/T003 — valid linked (non-nested) worktree is OWNED\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_valid_linked_worktree_is_owned(git_repo: Path, tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    worktree = _add_worktree(git_repo, tmp_path / \"linked-wt\", \"feature-a\")\n\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(worktree, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.OWNED\n    assert claim.opted_in is True\n    assert claim.claimed_checkout == worktree.resolve()\n    assert error_for_claim(claim) is None\n\n\ndef test_managed_linked_worktree_under_primary_is_owned(git_repo: Path) -> None:\n    worktrees_dir = git_repo / \".worktrees\"\n    worktrees_dir.mkdir()\n    worktree = _add_worktree(git_repo, worktrees_dir / \"linked-wt\", \"feature-managed\")\n\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(worktree, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.OWNED\n\n\ndef test_public_worktree_comparator_reuses_safe_commit_topology(\n    git_repo: Path, tmp_path: Path\n) -> None:\n    worktree = _add_worktree(git_repo, tmp_path / \"comparator-wt\", \"feature-compare\")\n\n    assert is_worktree_of(git_repo, worktree) is True\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# T003 — nested worktree (registry-based, not `.worktrees`-literal) is NESTED\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_nested_worktree_is_nested(git_repo: Path, tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    outer = _add_worktree(git_repo, tmp_path / \"outer-wt\", \"feature-outer\")\n    inner = _add_worktree(git_repo, outer / \"nested-inner-wt\", \"feature-inner\")\n\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(inner, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.NESTED\n    assert claim.opted_in is True\n    assert claim.detail\n    assert str(inner.resolve()) in claim.detail\n    assert str(outer.resolve()) in claim.detail\n\n    err = error_for_claim(claim)\n    assert isinstance(err, NestedCheckoutError)\n    assert err.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.NESTED\n\n\ndef test_nested_worktree_uses_generic_registry_not_dot_worktrees_literal(\n    git_repo: Path, tmp_path: Path\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"C-006: nested detection must work for paths with NO ``.worktrees`` segment.\n\n    ``outer``/``inner`` below live under a plain ``tmp_path`` tree — neither\n    path contains a literal ``.worktrees`` component, so a detector keyed on\n    that literal would miss this case entirely (the exact C-006 gap this WP\n    closes).\n    \"\"\"\n    outer = _add_worktree(git_repo, tmp_path / \"generic-outer\", \"feature-generic-outer\")\n    inner = _add_worktree(git_repo, outer / \"generic-inner\", \"feature-generic-inner\")\n    assert \".worktrees\" not in inner.parts\n\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(inner, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.NESTED\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# T004 — foreign repository (unrelated common-dir) is FOREIGN_OR_MISMATCHED\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_foreign_repo_is_foreign_or_mismatched(git_repo: Path, tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    foreign = tmp_path / \"foreign-repo\"\n    foreign.mkdir()\n    _run_git([\"init\"], cwd=foreign)\n    _run_git([\"config\", \"user.email\", \"test@example.com\"], cwd=foreign)\n    _run_git([\"config\", \"user.name\", \"Test User\"], cwd=foreign)\n    (foreign / \"README.md\").write_text(\"# Foreign Repo\\n\")\n    _run_git([\"add\", \"README.md\"], cwd=foreign)\n    _run_git([\"commit\", \"-m\", \"Initial commit\"], cwd=foreign)\n\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(foreign, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.FOREIGN_OR_MISMATCHED\n    assert claim.opted_in is True\n    assert claim.detail\n    assert str(foreign.resolve()) in claim.detail\n    assert str((foreign / \".git\").resolve()) in claim.detail\n    assert str((git_repo / \".git\").resolve()) in claim.detail\n\n    err = error_for_claim(claim)\n    assert isinstance(err, ForeignOrMismatchedCheckoutError)\n    assert err.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.FOREIGN_OR_MISMATCHED\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# T004 — corrupted/broken gitdir pointer is BROKEN_POINTER (fail-closed)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_broken_gitdir_pointer_is_broken_pointer(git_repo: Path, tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    worktree = _add_worktree(git_repo, tmp_path / \"to-corrupt-wt\", \"feature-corrupt\")\n\n    # Hand-corrupt the .git pointer file after creation (per WP guidance):\n    # point it at a gitdir that does not exist.\n    git_file = worktree / \".git\"\n    assert git_file.is_file()\n    git_file.write_text(\"gitdir: /nonexistent/path/.git/worktrees/to-corrupt-wt\\n\")\n\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(worktree, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.BROKEN_POINTER\n    assert claim.opted_in is True\n    assert claim.detail\n    assert str(worktree.resolve()) in claim.detail\n    assert str(git_repo.resolve()) in claim.detail\n\n    err = error_for_claim(claim)\n    assert isinstance(err, BrokenPointerCheckoutError)\n    assert err.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.BROKEN_POINTER\n\n\ndef test_missing_git_binary_is_broken_pointer(\n    git_repo: Path, tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A missing/unexecutable git binary must fold into BROKEN_POINTER, never raise.\"\"\"\n    worktree = _add_worktree(git_repo, tmp_path / \"no-git-binary-wt\", \"feature-no-git\")\n\n    def _raise_file_not_found(*args: object, **kwargs: object) -> object:\n        raise FileNotFoundError(\"git: command not found\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, \"run\", _raise_file_not_found)\n\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(worktree, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.BROKEN_POINTER\n    assert claim.detail\n    assert str(worktree.resolve()) in claim.detail\n    assert str(git_repo.resolve()) in claim.detail\n\n\ndef test_unavailable_worktree_registry_is_broken_pointer(\n    git_repo: Path, tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch\n) -> None:\n    worktree = _add_worktree(git_repo, tmp_path / \"registry-wt\", \"feature-registry\")\n\n    def _raise_registry_unavailable(repo_root: Path) -> frozenset[Path]:\n        raise WorktreeRegistryUnavailable(repo_root=repo_root, detail=\"registry failed\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(\n        checkout_ownership,\n        \"read_worktree_registry\",\n        _raise_registry_unavailable,\n    )\n\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(worktree, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.BROKEN_POINTER\n    assert claim.detail\n    assert str(worktree.resolve()) in claim.detail\n    assert str(git_repo.resolve()) in claim.detail\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# T001 — OwnershipClaim / OwnershipValidationResult / error vocabulary shape\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_ownership_validation_result_has_exactly_five_values() -> None:\n    assert {member.value for member in OwnershipValidationResult} == {\n        \"OWNED\",\n        \"UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN\",\n        \"NESTED\",\n        \"FOREIGN_OR_MISMATCHED\",\n        \"BROKEN_POINTER\",\n    }\n\n\ndef test_ownership_claim_is_frozen_dataclass(git_repo: Path) -> None:\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(git_repo, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n    assert isinstance(claim, OwnershipClaim)\n    with pytest.raises(FrozenInstanceError):\n        type(claim).__setattr__(claim, \"opted_in\", False)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"validation_result\", \"opted_in\", \"error_type\", \"error_code\"),\n    [\n        (\n            OwnershipValidationResult.UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN,\n            False,\n            UnownedNoOptInError,\n            \"WORKTREE_INVOCATION_REFUSED\",\n        ),\n        (\n            OwnershipValidationResult.NESTED,\n            True,\n            NestedCheckoutError,\n            \"OWNERSHIP_NESTED\",\n        ),\n        (\n            OwnershipValidationResult.FOREIGN_OR_MISMATCHED,\n            True,\n            ForeignOrMismatchedCheckoutError,\n            \"OWNERSHIP_FOREIGN\",\n        ),\n        (\n            OwnershipValidationResult.BROKEN_POINTER,\n            True,\n            BrokenPointerCheckoutError,\n            \"OWNERSHIP_BROKEN_POINTER\",\n        ),\n    ],\n)\ndef test_error_for_claim_exposes_cli_error_contract(\n    git_repo: Path,\n    validation_result: OwnershipValidationResult,\n    opted_in: bool,\n    error_type: type[CheckoutOwnershipError],\n    error_code: str,\n) -> None:\n    path = git_repo.resolve()\n    claim = OwnershipClaim(path, path, validation_result, opted_in, \"refused\")\n    error = error_for_claim(claim)\n    assert isinstance(error, error_type)\n    assert error.error_code == error_code\n    assert error.to_dict()[\"error_code\"] == error_code\n\n\ndef test_error_for_claim_returns_none_for_owned(git_repo: Path) -> None:\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(git_repo, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.OWNED\n    assert error_for_claim(claim) is None\n\n"}],"details":{"status":"ok"}}}

_run_git([\"config\", \"user.name\", \"Test User\"], cwd=repo)\n    (repo / \"README.md\").write_text(\"# Test Repo\\n\")\n    _run_git([\"add\", \"README.md\"], cwd=repo)\n    _run_git([\"commit\", \"-m\", \"Initial commit\"], cwd=repo)\n    _run_git([\"branch\", \"-M\", \"main\"], cwd=repo)\n    return repo\n\n\ndef _add_worktree(repo: Path, path: Path, branch: str) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Create a real linked worktree of ``repo`` at ``path`` on a new branch.\"\"\"\n    _run_git([\"worktree\", \"add\", \"-b\", branch, str(path)], cwd=repo)\n    return path\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# T002 — UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN (no claim, zero subprocess calls, NFR-001)\n# returns UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN with no git calls.\"\"\"\n    with patch(\"subprocess.run\") as run:\n        claim = resolve_ownership_claim(None, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN\n    assert claim.opted_in is False\n    assert claim.detail\n    assert str(git_repo.resolve()) in claim.detail\n    run.assert_not_called()\n\n\ndef test_no_claim_error_for_claim_maps_to_unowned_error(git_repo: Path) -> None:\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(None, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n    err = error_for_claim(claim)\n    assert isinstance(err, UnownedNoOptInError)\n    assert isinstance(err, CheckoutOwnershipError)\n    assert err.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# T002 — trivial self-ownership (primary claiming itself) is OWNED\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_primary_self_ownership_is_owned(git_repo: Path) -> None:\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(git_repo, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.OWNED\n    assert claim.opted_in is True\n    assert claim.claimed_checkout == git_repo.resolve()\n    assert claim.resolved_primary == git_repo.resolve()\n    assert error_for_claim(claim) is None\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# T002/T003 — valid is OwnershipValidationResult.OWNED\n    assert claim.opted_in is True\n    assert claim.claimed_checkout == worktree.resolve()\n    assert error_for_claim(claim) is None\n\n\ndef test_managed_linked_worktree_under_primary_is_owned(git_repo: Path) -> None:\n    worktrees_dir = git_repo / \".worktrees\"\n    worktrees_dir.mkdir()\n    worktree = _add_worktree(git_repo, worktrees_dir / \"linked-wt\", \"feature-managed\")\n\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(worktree, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.OWNED\n\n\ndef test_public_worktree_comparator_reuses_safe_commit_topology(\n    git_repo: Path, tmp_path: Path\n) -> None:\n    worktree = _add_worktree(git_repo, tmp_path / worktree (registry-based, not `.worktrees`-literal) is NESTED\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_nested_worktree_is_nested(git_repo: Path, claim = resolve_ownership_claim(inner, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.NESTED\n    assert claim.opted_in is True\n    assert assert err.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.NESTED\n\n\ndef test_nested_worktree_uses_generic_registry_not_dot_worktrees_literal(\n    git_repo: Path, tmp_path: Path\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"C-006: nested detection must work for paths with NO ``.worktrees`` segment.\n\n    ``outer``/``inner`` below live under a plain ``tmp_path`` tree — neither\n    path contains a literal ``.worktrees`` component, so a detector keyed on\n    that literal would miss this case entirely (the exact C-006 gap this WP\n    closes).\n    \"\"\"\n    outer = _add_worktree(git_repo, tmp_path / resolve_ownership_claim(inner, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.NESTED\n\n\n# \"Test User\"], cwd=foreign)\n    (foreign / \"README.md\").write_text(\"# Foreign Repo\\n\")\n    _run_git([\"add\", \"README.md\"], cwd=foreign)\n    _run_git([\"commit\", \"-m\", \"Initial \"no-git-binary-wt\", \"feature-no-git\")\n\n    def _raise_file_not_found(*args: object, **kwargs: object) -> object:\n        raise FileNotFoundError(\"git: command not found\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, \"run\", _raise_file_not_found)\n\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(worktree, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is These tests\nexercise :func:`resolve_ownership_claim` against REAL temporary git\nrepositories/worktrees (``tmp_path`` + real ``git init`` / ``git worktree\nadd`` subprocess calls) mirroring the house pattern in\n``tests/runtime/test_paths_unit.py`` and\n``tests/git_ops/test_safe_commit_helper_integration.py`` — no mocked git\noutput. dataclasses import FrozenInstanceError\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom unittest.mock import patch\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom specify_cli.core import checkout_ownership\nfrom specify_cli.core.checkout_ownership import (\n    BrokenPointerCheckoutError,\n    CheckoutOwnershipError,\n    ForeignOrMismatchedCheckoutError,\n    NestedCheckoutError,\n    OwnershipClaim,\n _run_git(args: list[str], cwd: Path) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [\"git\", *args],\n        cwd=cwd,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        encoding=\"utf-8\",\n        errors=\"replace\",\n        check=True,\n    )\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef git_repo(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Create a real, initialized git repository with one commit.\"\"\"\n    repo = tmp_path / \"primary\"\n    repo.mkdir()\n    _run_git([\"init\"], cwd=repo)\n    _run_git([\"config\", \"user.email\", \"test@example.com\"], cwd=repo)\n    _run_git([\"config\", \"user.name\", \"Test User\"], cwd=repo)\n    (repo / \"README.md\").write_text(\"# Test Repo\\n\")\n    _run_git([\"add\", \"README.md\"], cwd=repo)\n    _run_git([\"commit\", \"-m\", \"Initial commit\"], cwd=repo)\n    _run_git([\"branch\", \"-M\", \"main\"], cwd=repo)\n    return repo\n\n\ndef _add_worktree(repo: Path, path: Path, branch: str) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Create a real linked worktree of ``repo`` at ``path`` on a new branch.\"\"\"\n    _run_git([\"worktree\", \"add\", \"-b\", branch, str(path)], cwd=repo)\n    return path\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# T002 — UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN (no claim, zero subprocess calls, NFR-001)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_no_claim_returns_unowned_no_opt_in(\n    git_repo: Path,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"``claimed_checkout=None`` returns UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN with no git calls.\"\"\"\n    with patch(\"subprocess.run\") as run:\n        claim = resolve_ownership_claim(None, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN\n    assert claim.opted_in is False\n    assert claim.detail\n    assert str(git_repo.resolve()) in claim.detail\n    run.assert_not_called()\n\n\ndef test_no_claim_error_for_claim_maps_to_unowned_error(git_repo: Path) -> None:\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(None, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n    err = error_for_claim(claim)\n    assert isinstance(err, UnownedNoOptInError)\n    assert isinstance(err, CheckoutOwnershipError)\n    assert err.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# T002 — trivial self-ownership (primary claiming itself) is OWNED\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_primary_self_ownership_is_owned(git_repo: Path) -> None:\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(git_repo, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.OWNED\n    assert claim.opted_in is True\n    assert claim.claimed_checkout == git_repo.resolve()\n    assert claim.resolved_primary == git_repo.resolve()\n    assert error_for_claim(claim) is None\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# T002/T003 — valid linked (non-nested) worktree is OWNED\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef test_valid_linked_worktree_is_owned(git_repo: Path, tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    worktree = _add_worktree(git_repo, tmp_path / \"linked-wt\", \"feature-a\")\n\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(worktree, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.OWNED\n    assert claim.opted_in is True\n    assert claim.claimed_checkout == worktree.resolve()\n    assert error_for_claim(claim) is None\n\n\ndef test_managed_linked_worktree_under_primary_is_owned(git_repo: Path) -> None:\n    worktrees_dir = git_repo / \".worktrees\"\n    worktrees_dir.mkdir()\n    worktree = _add_worktree(git_repo, worktrees_dir / \"linked-wt\", \"feature-managed\")\n\n    claim = resolve_ownership_claim(worktree, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.OWNED\n\n\ndef test_public_worktree_comparator_reuses_safe_commit_topology(\n    git_repo: Path, tmp_path: Path\n) -> None:\n    worktree = _add_worktree(git_repo, tmp_path / claim = resolve_ownership_claim(inner, resolved_primary=git_repo)\n\n    assert claim.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.NESTED\n    assert claim.opted_in is True\n    assert assert err.validation_result is OwnershipValidationResult.NESTED\n\n\ndef test_nested_worktree_uses_generic_registry_not_dot_worktrees_literal(\n    git_repo: Path, tmp_path: Path\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"C-006: nested detection must work for paths with NO ``.worktrees`` segment.\n\n    ``outer``/``inner`` below live under a plain ``tmp_path`` tree — neither\n    path contains a literal {"type":"tool_execution_update","toolCallId":"functions.ipython:12","toolName":"ipython","args":{"code":"dm = open(spec_dir+\"/data-model.md\").read()\nprint(dm[:4000])"},"partialResult":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Data Model: Worktree-Owned Root for Mission Create/Next\n\n**Mission**: `worktree-owned-root-3328-01KZRG01` | **Issue**: [#3328](https://github.com/Priivacy-ai/spec-kitty/issues/3328)\n\nThis mission has no persisted business data model (it is a CLI/runtime-topology fix). This document instead models the **checkout-ownership domain concepts** the implementation must reason about precisely — entities, their attributes, and the relationships/validation rules between them, derived from the code inventory in `research.md`.\n\n## Entities\n\n### `Checkout`\n\nA single git working directory — either the primary checkout or a linked worktree.\n\n| Attribute | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| `path` | absolute path | The checkout's working directory root. |\n| `git_common_dir` | absolute path | Result of `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` run from `path`, resolved to absolute. Shared by every checkout of the same repository. |\n| `toplevel` | absolute path | Result of `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` run from `path`. |\n| `is_primary` | bool | True iff `path == git_common_dir.parent` (the checkout that owns `.git` as a real directory, not a `gitdir:` pointer file). |\n| `gitdir_pointer_target` | absolute path \\| None | For a linked worktree, the target of the `.git` file's `gitdir:` line (e.g. `<primary>/.git/worktrees/<name>`). `None` for the primary checkout. |\n\n**Existing code that computes these attributes** (research D-2, D-4): `is_worktree_context()`, `_is_worktree_of()`, `locate_project_root()`, `resolve_canonical_repo_root()` — each recomputes a subset independently; the plan should route new validation through `_is_worktree_of`'s comparison rather than adding a sixth implementation.\n\n### `OwnershipClaim`\n\nThe explicit, per-invocation declaration that a `Checkout` should be treated as the mission's write root.\n\n| Attribute | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| `claimed_checkout` | `Checkout` | The checkout the caller has explicitly named (new — does not exist today). |\n| `resolved_primary` | `Checkout` | The canonical common-repository checkout, resolved independently of the claim (via the existing `locate_project_root`/`get_main_repo_root` family). |\n| `validation_result` | `OwnershipValidationResult` (enum, below) | Outcome of comparing `claimed_checkout` against `resolved_primary`'s topology. |\n| `opted_in` | bool | Whether the caller supplied the new explicit-ownership affordance at all. When `False`, today's existing fail-closed default behavior (research D-1) applies unchanged — no `OwnershipClaim` is constructed. |\n\n### `OwnershipValidationResult` (enum)\n\nThe five possible validation outcomes (spec.md Key Entities, User Story 2's acceptance scenarios):\n\n| Value | Meaning | Existing precedent |\n|---|---|---|\n| `OWNED` | `claimed_checkout`'s `git_common_dir` matches `resolved_primary`'s `git_common_dir`, and `claimed_checkout` is not nested inside any other worktree per the registry. Accepted. | `_is_worktree_of()` returning `True`, plus a new nested-worktree negative check (research D-4). |\n| `UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN` | Caller did not supply the ownership affordance; today's existing refusal (mission create) or ambient behavior (next) applies unchanged. | Existing `is_worktree_context()` / `require_main_repo` behavior — UNCHANGED (C-001, FR-004). |\n| `NESTED` | `claimed_checkout`'s path is a descendant of another worktree's root per `git worktree list --porcelain`. Refused. | New — built on `coordination/surface_resolver.read_worktree_registry()`'s raw entries (research D-4), not its `.worktrees`-literal `_enclosing_worktree_root()`. |\n| `FOREIGN_OR_MISMATCHED` | `claimed_checkout`'s `git_common_dir` does not match `resolved_primary`'s. Refused, common-dir named in the error. | `_is_worktree_of()` returning `False` on a common-dir mismatch. |\n| `BROKEN_POINTER` | `claimed_checkout`'s `.git` file exists but its `gitdir:` target is missing/unreadable, or any underlying git subprocess failed. Refused (fail-closed, NFR-004). | New — must not \n"}],"details":{"status":"ok"}}}

Contract: Explicit Checkout-Ownership Affordance\n\n**Mission**: `worktree-owned-root-3328-01KZRG01` | **Issue**: [#3328](https://github.com/Priivacy-ai/spec-kitty/issues/3328)\n\nThis contract defines the CLI/API surface the implementation phase (WPs) must deliver. It is a specification of observable behavior — exact flag names/wording are implementation-phase decisions the tasks phase may refine, but the request/response shape and refusal taxonomy below are binding.\n\n## CLI Surface: `spec-kitty agent mission create`\n\n### New option\n\n```\n--owned-checkout PATH   Explicitly declare PATH as a linked worktree this invocation\n                         owns. Validated via git topology (common-dir + worktree\n                         registry) before acceptance. Mutually exclusive with running\n                         from an unowned worktree without this flag (existing refusal\n                         is unchanged when this flag is absent).\n```\n\n### Behavior contract\n\n| Precondition | `--owned-checkout` supplied? | Outcome |\n|---|---|---|\n| CWD is the primary checkout | No | Unchanged — succeeds as today. |\n| CWD is the primary checkout | Yes, path == CWD | Succeeds (trivial self-ownership case, mirrors `safe_commit`'s `repo_root == worktree_root` contract). |\n| CWD is a linked worktree (any path) | No | Unchanged — refuses with today's `MissionCreationError` (\"Cannot create missions from inside a worktree…\"). |\n| CWD is a linked worktree, path is a validly-linked, non-nested worktree of the resolved primary | Yes, path == CWD | Succeeds. Mission files, coordination/lane refs land under `path`. Primary checkout and every other worktree remain untouched. |\n| Path is nested inside another worktree's checkout | Yes | Refuses. Error is structurally distinguishable as `NESTED` (see Error Taxonomy). |\n| Path's git common-dir does not match the resolved primary's | Yes | Refuses. Error is structurally distinguishable as `FOREIGN_OR_MISMATCHED`, naming both common-dirs. |\n| Path's `.git` file exists but its `gitdir:` target is unreadable/missing | Yes | Refuses. Error is structurally distinguishable as `BROKEN_POINTER`. |\n| Any underlying `git rev-parse`/`git worktree list` subprocess fails | Yes | Refuses (fail-closed, NFR-004) — never falls back to unvalidated acceptance. |\n\n### `--json` payload shape (success)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"success\": true,\n  \"mission_slug\": \"...\",\n  \"owned_checkout\": \"/abs/path/to/worktree\",\n  \"canonical_repo_root\": \"/abs/path/to/primary\",\n  ...\n}\n```\n\n### `--json` payload shape (refusal)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"success\": false,\n  \"error_code\": \"OWNERSHIP_NESTED\" | \"OWNERSHIP_FOREIGN\" | \"OWNERSHIP_BROKEN_POINTER\" | \"WORKTREE_INVOCATION_REFUSED\",\n  \"error\": \"<human-readable message naming the specific checkouts/paths involved>\"\n}\n```\n\n`WORKTREE_INVOCATION_REFUSED` is the existing (unchanged) refusal code for the no-opt-in case — this contract does not rename or restructure it (regression risk called out in plan.md IC-04).\n\n## CLI Surface: `spec-kitty next`\n\n### New option\n\n```\n--owned-checkout PATH   Same semantics as `mission create`'s flag. When supplied and\n                         validated OWNED, `next` roots per-checkout runtime state\n                         (feature-runs.json, merge-lock directory) at PATH instead of\n                         the ambiently-resolved primary checkout.\n```\n\n### Behavior contract\n\n| Precondition | `--owned-checkout` supplied? | Outcome |\n|---|---|---|\n| CWD is a `.worktrees/<name>` path (today's `require_main_repo` detects this) | No | Unchanged — refuses exactly as today. |\n| CWD is a generic linked worktree (today's `require_main_repo` does NOT detect this) | No | Unchanged — behaves exactly as today (ambient resolution to primary; NOT retrofitted into a new refusal — spec.md Acceptance Scenario, User Story 2 #4). |\n| CWD is a validly-linked, non-nested worktree | Yes, path == CWD | Succeeds. Mission decision resolves against the mission stored at the owned checkout; runtime-state files (`feature-runs.json` equivalent) are read/written under the owned checkout's own `.kittify/runtime/`. |\n| Nested / foreign / broken-pointer (same taxonomy as `mission create`) | Yes | Refuses with the same structured error codes. |\n\n## Error Taxonomy (shared by both surfaces)\n\n| `error_code` | `OwnershipValidationResult` (data-model.md) | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| `WORKTREE_INVOCATION_REFUSED` | `UNOWNED_NO_OPT_IN` | Existing, unchanged refusal — caller did not opt in. |\n| `OWNERSHIP_NESTED` | `NESTED` | The claimed checkout is nested inside another worktree's own directory tree. |\n| `OWNERSHIP_FOREIGN` | `FOREIGN_OR_MISMATCHED` | The claimed checkout's git common-dir does not match the resolved primary's. |\n| `OWNERSHIP_BROKEN_POINTER` | `BROKEN_POINTER` | The claimed checkout's `.git` gitdir pointer is unreadable, missing its target, or a git subprocess failed while validating it. |\n\n## Non-Goals of This Contract\n\n- Does not define `#3128`'s post-ownership caller-vs-declared-workspace comparison (that guard consumes this contract's validated `OwnershipClaim` as an input, in a separate mission).\n- Does not add any new production `allow_worktree_context=True` call site (NFR-003) — `--owned-checkout` is a wholly independent, validated parameter.\n- Does not change behavior for any caller that omits `--owned-checkout` (C-001/C-002).\n\n"}],"details":{"durationMs":7,"status":"ok","stdout":"# Contract: Explicit Checkout-Ownership Affordance\n\n**Mission**: `worktree-owned-root-3328-01KZRG01` | **Issue**: [#3328](https://github.com/Priivacy-ai/spec-kitty/issues/3328)\n\nThis contract defines the CLI/API surface the implementation phase (WPs) must deliver.
